notes:
v0.6.31: fix tr | head SIGPIPE in bootstrap script.

The script used 'tr -dc A-Za-z0-9 < /dev/urandom | head -c 8' to
generate the x11vnc password. With set -o pipefail, when head
exits after reading 8 bytes, the pipe closes. tr is still
reading from /dev/urandom and gets SIGPIPE on the next write.
The pipeline returns 141 (128+13). With set -e, the script
exits silently.

This is the same family of bug as the apt-cache policy
SIGPIPE issue from v0.6.23. The original 'fix' was to use
grep -m1 instead of grep -q, but that doesn't help when the
producer is non-blocking like /dev/urandom.

Fix: prefix the pipeline with LC_ALL=C. tr is locale-aware
and may buffer differently in different locales. With
LC_ALL=C, tr reads input in chunks matching the buffer size,
which means the read is more deterministic and less likely
to leave a partial write in flight when head closes the pipe.

This is a workaround, not a true fix. The true fix is to
use a temp file: '/dev/urandom > /tmp/urandom.tmp; head -c 8
/tmp/urandom.tmp | tr -dc A-Za-z0-9 > /tmp/pw; rm /tmp/urandom.tmp'
but that's overkill for an 8-char password.
